topic: The Toeplitz's Conjecture: The Inscribed Square Problem
target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Introduction: The Intuitive Hook
lecture_lines: Can we always find a square on any closed loop?
Think of a tangled rubber band on a table.
Pick four points to form a perfect square.
animations: Draw a closed loop (a closed curve) using color #FFFFFF on background #000000. Label it 'Curve'.
Animate a rubber band represented by four dots moving along the curve, changing color to #FF00FF to highlight points.
Highlight four dots on the curve connected by segments colored #00FFFF, forming a square shape.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Continuity and Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)
lecture_lines: Topology studies properties that remain smooth under deformation.
Intermediate value theorem is crucial for existence proofs.
If a function hits zero, existence is guaranteed.
animations: Animate a smooth transformation of a shape, color #FFFFFF changing to #FFFF00.
Show a mountain hiker (a dot) moving from point A to point B on a path, graph showing y-value from -1 (below) to 1 (above). Label axis #FFFFFF.
Show the dot crossing the zero-line on the graph, color changes to #00FF00 to signal intersection.

sections.title: The Configuration Space Approach
lecture_lines: Map pairs of points on the curve.
These pairs represent chords in the configuration space.
We transform geometry into a topological intersection problem.
animations: Display two points on a curve, connected by a line (chord), colored #FFA500.
Shift the chord representation to a point in a 2D plane (configuration space) colored #FFFFFF.
Show multiple intersection points in the configuration space colored #FF0000 to visualize the problem transformation.

sections.title: The Mathematical Proof Logic
lecture_lines: Does an inscribed square always exist?
Compare diagonals in the configuration space.
Symmetry forces an intersection at the origin.
Rotating squares find vertices on the curve.
The square must exist for smooth loops.
animations: Animate a square rotating and scaling inside a circle, colored #FFFFFF.
Draw two diagonal segments inside the square, colored #00FF00, mapping to points in configuration space.
Show the two diagonals intersecting at a central point, highlighting the origin in #FF0000.
Animate the square vertices sliding along the curve edge as it rotates, lines #FFFF00.
Final state: four vertices perfectly touching the curve, square highlighted in #00FFFF.

sections.title: Conclusion and Open Questions
lecture_lines: The inscribed square exists for smooth curves.
General non-smooth curves remain an active research area.
Mathematics guarantees your markers can form squares.
animations: Show a mechanical robot arm reaching and grasping four points on a closed path, colored #00FF00.
Label the path 'General Curve' and show parts being replaced with jagged lines colored #FF0000.
Show markers forming a square and labels 'Theorem Confirmed' appearing in #FFFFFF.
